questions.question: Which of the following is the most reactive metal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Potassium (K) is a most reactive metal and reacts vigorously with air and water.

 
 
• A large amount of heat is produced in their reaction.
 
• To avoid such accidents this metal is kept immersed in kerosene oil.
 
• Potassium undergoes a reaction with water similar to that of sodium; the products of the reaction are potassium hydroxide and hydrogen gas. 
 
• This reaction releases a great deal of heat energy, often igniting the hydrogen gas that is produced.
 
 
 
• Sodium (Na) and Lithium (Li) are also very reactive to air and water and need to be stored under oil to prevent them from reacting with gases in the air and water.
 
• Caesium (Cs) is the most reactive of all metals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Metals react with water and oxygen present in the air. 
 
• Metal with higher reactivity has vigorous reactions. 
 
• For example, sodium catches fire in the air, hence it is kept in kerosene oil. 
 
• Due to such reactivity of metals, most of the metals are not available in nature in a free state. 
 
• They are present in form of their compounds (oxides, carbonates, sulphides etc,)
 
• Few metals which are least reactive are available in a free state. 
 
• Such metals are gold, silver, Platinum

questions.question: Which of the following elements can be used to treat/purify water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Chlorine.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorine **elements can be used to treat/purify water.
 
• **Chlorination** is one of many methods that can be used to disinfect water.
 
• It is a chemical disinfection method that uses various types of chlorine or chlorine-containing substances for the oxidation and disinfection of what will be the potable water source.
 
• **Chlorine inactivates a microorganism by damaging its cell membrane. Once the cell membrane is weakened, chlorine can enter the cell and disrupt cell respiration and DNA activity.**
 
• The main objective of this chlorine addition is to disinfect the water and maintain chlorine residuals that will remain in the water as it travels through the distribution system.
 
• Any type of chlorine that is added to water during the treatment process will result in the formation of hypochlorous acid (HOCI) and hypochlorite ions (OCI-), which are the main disinfecting compounds in chlorinated water.
 
• The amount of chlorine that is required to disinfect water is dependent on the impurities in the water that needs to be treated.
 
• Chlorination is able to provide a residual to reduce the chance of pathogen regrowth in water storage tanks or within the water distribution system.
 
• Chlorination has been proven to be very effective against bacteria and viruses.
 
• However, it cannot disinfect all waterborne pathogens. Certain pathogens, namely protozoan cysts, are resistant to the effects of chlorine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chlorine** was first discovered in** Sweden in 1744.**
 
• At that time, people believed that odors from the water were responsible for transmitting diseases.
 
• Chlorination can be done at any time/point throughout the water treatment process. There is not one specific time when chlorine must be added.

questions.question: Which of the following is a radioisotope of hydrogen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tritium.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **rare and radioactive isotope of hydrogen** is known as** tritium or hydrogen-3.**
 
• **One proton and two neutrons** make up the tritium atom's nucleus.
 
• On Earth, tritium occurs** naturally very rarely.**
 
• There are very **small amounts in the atmospher**e, which are created when the** gases interact with cosmic rays.**
 
• By **exposing lithium metal or lithium-containing ceramic pebbles** to radiation in a nuclear reactor, it can be created **artificially.**
 
• Tritium is used as the energy source in **radioluminescent lights for watches, gun sights, and numerous instruments** and tools.
 
• It serves as a **radioactive tracer **in **scientific and medicinal settings.**
 
• Along with the more **accessible deuterium**, tritium is also employed as** a nuclear fusion fuel** in tokamak reactors and hydrogen bombs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xenon:**

 
 
• Xenon has the **atomic number 54 **and the **symbol Xe.**
 
• It is a** thick, colourless, and odourless noble gas** that is present in minute levels in Earth's atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Technetium:**
 
 
• The chemical element** technetium** has the **atomic number 43 and Tc** as its symbol.
 
• It is the lightest element with** radioactive isotopes.**
 
 
 
• **Thorium:**
 
 
• Thorium is a **metallic chemical element **with low** radioactivity.**
 
• It has the** atomic number 90** and the **symbol Th.**

questions.question: Which one of the following pair is an example of Isobars?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Calcium and argon__.

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Calcium and argon are examples of a pair of Isobars**__. Calcium and argon have a mass number of 40. The atomic number of argon 18 and an atomic number of calcium is 20.
 
• Isobars:
 __
 
• These are atoms of the elements having the **same mass number but different atomic numbers**.
 
• They differ in the chemical property but has the same physical property.
 
• Example: argon, potassium and calcium.
 
 
 
• The mass number is the sum of a number of protons and neutrons in an atom of the elements is called the mass number.
 
 
• It is denoted by A.
 
 
 
• The atomic number is the number of proton or electrons in an atom of the element is called the atomic number.
 
 
• It is denoted by Z.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Isotopes: These are atoms of the elements having the same atomic number but a different mass number.

 
 
• The isotopes of hydrogen are Protium, Deuterium and Tritium
 
 
 
• Isotones: These are atoms of different elements having the same number of neutrons.
 
• Isoelectronic: These are atoms/molecules/ ions containing the same number of electrons.

questions.question: Which of the following chemicals are vastly used in the gunpowder of fireworks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium nitrate, sulphur and charcoal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Gunpowder**

 
 
• It was the** first chemical explosive **and the only one known until the invention of** nitrocellulose, nitroglycerin, smokeless powder, and TNT in the second half of the 19th century.**
 
• Before the invention of gunpowder, many incendiary and burning devices had been used, including Greek fire.
 
• **Roger Bacon invented gunpowder.**
 
• Bacon explored the manufacture of** gunpowder (also known as black powder).**
 
• It consists of a mixture of** sulfur, charcoal, and potassium nitrate (saltpetre).**
 
• Sulfur and charcoal act as fuels while the saltpetre is an oxidizer.
 
• **Bacon **was the **first one in Europe to explain the explosive force of gunpowder.**

questions.question: Which formula is used to represent the three-dimensional structures of molecules using a two-dimensional surface like a sheet of paper or a computer screen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Dash-wedge formula.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The wedge and dash notation is used to represent three-dimensional structures of molecules using a two-dimensional surface, like a sheet of paper or a computer screen.
 
• This type of structure is also called **wedge-dash notation or wedges-and-dash notation.**
 
• It is commonly used in organic chemistry, though you may see it any time a molecule structure is given.
 
• **Wedges –** Solid triangular wedges represent chemical bonds and groups that are coming out of the page, toward you.
 
• **Dashes –** Dashed triangular shapes represent chemical bonds and groups extending back behind the page.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bond Line Formula:**

 
 
• A bond line structural formula is another way of structural representation of organic compounds.
 
• Here, every bond is represented as a line in a zigzag manner.
 
• If not specified, every terminal is assumed to be a **methyl (-CH3) group.**
 
 
 
• **Lewis structure formula :**
 
 
• The Lewis structure, also known as an electron fleck structure, is a diagrammatic representation of determining the total number of valence electrons present in a snippet that are ready to form bonds to form a patch and, ultimately, an emulsion.
 
 
 
• **Condensed structural formula:**
 
 
• In the condensed structural formula, every carbon atom is represented individually, and the following carbon atoms are placed to the atoms that are bonded to that particular carbon atom.

questions.question: Which of the following kitchen substances can be used as an ‘olfactory indicator’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ Onion.__

__
 
• An **olfactory indicator** is a substance whose **smell varies depending** on whether it is** mixed with an acidic** or **basic solution**.
 
• Olfactory indicators can be used in the **laboratory** to test whether a **solution **is a** base** or an **acid**, a process called **olfactory titration**.
 
• Those substances whose** smell odor** **changes** in **acidic** or **basic** solution are called** olfactory indicators.**
 
• **Onion extract** and **Vanilla extract** are the types of olfactory indicator.
 
• **Two substances are :**
 
 
• **​Onion** has a **great** smell when a basic solution of **sodium hydroxide solution** is added, the** onion smell cannot be detected**. But an **acidic solution** like **HCL** does not **destroy the smell of onion.**
 
• **Vanilla** has a **characteristic smell**. If a basic solution like** sodium hydroxide** is added to** vanilla**, it **can't detect its smell**. But an acidic solution like **HCL** does not **destroy the smell of vanilla extract.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Five to eight per cent solution of acetic acid in water is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**vinegar.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vinegar **is a combination of acetic acid and water made by a two-step fermentation process.
 
• First, yeast feed on the sugar or starch of any liquid from a plant food such as fruits, whole grains, potatoes, or rice.
 
• This liquid ferments into alcohol.
 
• The alcohol is then exposed to oxygen and the acetic acid bacteria Acetobacter to ferment again over weeks or months, forming vinegar. 
 
• **Vinegar** contains five to eight per cent solution of acetic acid in water.
 
• Vinegar is an essential component of most pickling brines, whereas acetic acid also functions as a natural preservative.
 
• Vinegar is also used to stimulate chemical reactions that take place during cooking and baking.
 
• Vinegar is also frequently used in marinades because the acid helps tenderize meat by breaking down its fibre.
 
• Distilled vinegar has traditionally been used as a disinfectant in the home.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lime or quicklime:**

 
 
• Calcium oxide, CaO, also known as lime or more specifically quicklime, is a white or greyish white solid produced in large quantities by roasting calcium carbonate so as to drive off carbon dioxide.
 
• At room temperature, CaO will spontaneously absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, reversing the reaction.
 
• It will also absorb water, converting itself into calcium hydroxide and releasing heat in the process.
 
• The bubbling that accompanies the reaction is the source of its name as “quick,” or living, lime. 
 
 
 
• **Alcohol:**
 
 
• Alcohol is a type of organic compound that carries at least one hydroxyl functional group (−OH) bound to a saturated carbon atom.
 
• The term alcohol originally referred to the primary alcohol ethanol (ethyl alcohol), which is used as a drug and is the main alcohol present in alcoholic drinks.

questions.question: What is the atomic number of nitrogen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• ATOMIC NUMBER: 

 
 
• ​It is defined as the number of protons present in the nucleus.
 
• It is denoted by the letter Z.
 
 
 
• MASS NUMBER: 
 
 
• ​The total number of protons and neutrons present in a nucleus is called the mass number of the element.
 
• It is denoted by the letter A.
 
 
 
• **For neutral atom,**
 
 
• Number of protons in an atom = Z
 
• Number of electrons in an atom = Z
 
• Number of nucleons in an atom = A
 
• Number of neutrons in an atom = N = A – Z
 
 

CALCULATION__:

 
• Given – A = 14 and Number of electrons in an atom (e) = 7
 
• As we know that the number of protons is equal to the number of electrons in an atom. Therefore, the number of protons is 7.
 
• 
 
As we know that, Mass number (A) = Number of protons (p) + Number of neutrons (n)

 
∴ n = A – p

 ⇒ n = 14 – 7 = **7**

questions.question: Deuterium and tritium are:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Isotopes of Hydrogen.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deuterium and tritium are Isotopes of Hydrogen.**
 
• Isotopes are different forms of the same element that contain an equal number of protons but different numbers of neutrons in their nuclei, and hence differ in relative atomic mass but not in chemical properties.
 
• Hydrogen has three isotopes:** Hydrogen (1 proton and 0 neutrons), Deuterium (1 proton and 1 neutron) and Tritium (1 proton and 2 neutrons).**
 
• Out of the three, **tritium **is a very rare isotope and is also radioactive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ISOTOPES:**

 
 
• Atoms with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons are called isotopes.
 
• They are elements with the same atomic number but different mass numbers since the atomic number equal the number of protons and the atomic mass equal the sum of protons and neutrons.
 
• Isotopes are various forms of the same element.
 
• Protium 1H1, deuterium 1H2 or D, and finally tritium 1H3 or T are the three hydrogen isotopes.
 
• There are no neutrons in protium, but one neutron is present in deuterium and two neutrons are present in tritium.
 
• Protium is the most common type of hydrogen, with deuterium accounting for 0.0156 per cent of all hydrogen on the planet's surface.
 
• The concentration of tritium is one atom per 1018 protium atoms.
 
• The only tritium, out of these three hydrogen isotopes, is radioactive in nature and releases low-energy b particles.

questions.question: In a neutralisation reaction, a new substance is formed, called _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The neutralization reaction is the reaction between an** acid and a base where both neutralise the effect of each other**.
 
• In this reaction, **heat is always produced, or evolved**.
 
• In the neutralisation reaction, a new substance is formed is called salt.
 
• ***Acid+Base → Salt+Water (Heat is evolved)***
 
• For example -** Hydrochloric acid (HCl) + Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) →Sodium chloride (NaCl) + Water (H2O)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
